title: The library plan: every document into the record by a queue of small agents, then no PDFs
body:
**Every document the record draws on is read page by page into the tables - each fact once, cited to its source and page, cross-checked against the car - and then the PDFs leave the tree. The new project `05-library` runs it with a queue many small agents work at once, most valuable pages first across all documents. Phases 0 (structure) and 1 (inventory) are done; phase 2 waits on Camden's go.**

Camden's words (chat, 2026-10-14): "now make a clear perfect task list for yourself ... to parse the rest of the pdf files into text data and crossreference and encorperate into the car data proper. when you are done there should be no pdfs but a master reference page in the manual with all the links to the pdfs. all the data in the car folder should be photos, cad models, easy to manipulate one fact once well organized incosistacy proof data stystem." Then: "follow all recomendations, and complete phase 0 and 1, then repost back to me before we continue. ensure you document the full agent plan ... this should be an agent only edited file that should aid many agents concurently parsiing most valuble secions first out of each pdf not pdf by pdf. each agent should easily just scan for the next not done or in progress item on the list then mark in progress and begin. these should be very small cheep agents with low cache just to scan one small thing. record the full plan for this prosses and prepare everything for parsing and we will play with the plan more before we begin".

His rulings, each the recommendation he accepted: (A) an offline copy of every PDF outside the tree before any is deleted; (B) a figure becomes rows plus a link to its page, a cropped image only where the picture is the information; (C) this car and the other 1979-85 years as held-back rows, other models only indexed; (D) the same rule in every project; (E) the model library stays in 02-cad; (F) git history left alone, the repository private as D-524 ruled (his GitHub setting).

How it is built (the whole plan: `rx7.py doc library`):

- **The agent-only file is the `queue` table** of 05-library, edited only through `rx7.py claim` (takes the highest priority open item, marks it claimed with the agent and the time) and `rx7.py finish` (marks it done or failed, with a result). Every writing command of `rx7.py` now holds one tree-wide lock for its whole read-change-write, so any number of agents can claim and write at once without losing a row; a claim abandoned for 90 minutes is handed out again. A table, not a Markdown list, because a list file edited by many agents loses edits, and because the table is checked like the rest of the record and the app shows it.
- **Most valuable first, across documents**: each item is a few pages of one document sharing a section, scored by the document's tier (1 this car's own data .. 5 index only), unread over cited, this car over other years over other models, troubleshooting and tables over prose, a document's front first. The head of the queue is every troubleshooting table, then the 1981-83 data and the parts catalogue, then the 1985 and 1983 manuals' unread tables.
- **Small cheap workers**: a worker reads only `rx7.py playbook parse` (two pages), claims one item, reads its pages with `page.py` (text, or an image for drawings), writes what they state as staged `facts` rows (`add id=next`, no id to choose, no table to search), marks its pages, finishes the item, and stops. It never searches the record, never runs git. The merge (phase 3, `playbook merge`, a stronger model) moves each fact into its home table once, marks duplicates and raises conflicts.
- **New 00-CAR tables**: `docs` (each PDF file: its source, path, pages, checksum, text layer, owner, tier, scope, whether it is on disk), `pages` (each page: kind, topic, scope, status, the rows holding its facts - the coverage map), `diagnosis` (the troubleshooting tables). `check` refuses a page naming a missing row or misnumbered, a document marked gone with an unfinished page or still on disk, and a queue item claimed or done without its agent or time; `rx7.py dups` lists the 36 specs that already hold one fact twice, for phase 3.

Phase 1, done: 163 PDFs (4,116 pages) as docs and pages rows; 95 sources rows added for files no row named (the 1983 Mitchell manual among them); 687 pages already cited by the record, marked with the rows citing them; 13 duplicate files (393 pages) marked; 1,229 queue items built (tier 1: 482 items, 1,349 pages).

Phase 2 starts only when Camden says so. Subagents are used for it by his design here; until he says begin, none runs.

title: Sessions: a manager script, one call per item, every item priced and capped
body:
**The library's sessions are hour-long runs of a manager script; every queue item already carries its model, its predicted tokens and dollars, and a generous hard cap. A worker is one `claude -p` call with no access to the tree; the manager does every write.** This refines how D-574 runs; its plan stands.

Camden's words (chat, 2026-10-14): "help me gauge what a reasonable limmit is for each bot giving them the generous side (they should have just over expected tokens to finish task) so if somthing goes wrong it doesnt finish but only if something goes wrong like a loop, we will size the main run in time for now we will run hour long sessions where one manager makes all the sub models to handle one small task cheap and clean. please ensure before we begin every section is already maped and given a pridiced cost and chosen model to prossess it. then the manages can cheeply just follow the plan and make the right model and give them the right generous limit for one hour (stops spawning new agents but luts ones going finish). the map is everything that should make this prosses ass cheep as it can be".

- **The manager is a script** (`05-library/tools/run_session.py`), so managing costs nothing: for the session's minutes it keeps N workers running, most valuable item first; then it starts nothing new, lets the running ones finish, checks, commits and pushes, and prints the ledger.
- **A worker** is handed its pages' text in the prompt and reads only the page images it is given; it answers with facts and pages blocks. Started in an empty folder, it loads no CLAUDE.md and no memory. One measured bare Haiku call: 34,000 tokens of fixed context, $0.0027.
- **Every item is priced** by `build_queue.py`'s cost model (its constants in one place, recalibrated from each session's actual tokens and dollars, which the queue now records): Haiku 5.5 for text and scanned prose (1,093 items, $4.44 predicted), Sonnet 5.5 for drawings, the catalogue's figures, wiring, reviews and merges (136 items, $16.16); the cap is three times the prediction, never under $0.03 (Haiku) or $0.40 (Sonnet), enforced by `claude -p --max-budget-usd`.
- The parse playbook is now the worker's prompt text; the plan (`rx7.py doc library`) says how a session runs and what to check after it.

title: Parsing only stores; one overhaul merges everything at the end
body:
**No merging during parsing. Parsing only stores: every fact of every page goes into 05-library's `facts` table (and each page's kind, topic, scope and status into 00-CAR `pages`), which is the library's whole non-PDF copy. Cross-referencing, combining and merging into 00-CAR and the projects is one separate task (L3, the overhaul) after every page is parsed, planned and priced then.**

Camden's words (chat, 2026-10-14): "can we leave all merging for now and just store all the data in a non pdf format then later do one ovehall and crossreference and combine and prossess all the info and merg it into car once at the end as a seperate task".

Why it is better as well as cheaper now: the overhaul sees every document's facts at once, so a fact stated by the 1980, 1982 and 1985 books and the catalogue is combined once with all its sources, which item-by-item merging could not do. The merge playbook and `build_queue.py --merge` stay as tools for that task, to be redesigned with it. The PDFs stay on disk until the overhaul and the References page are done (L6 already waits on L3).

title: The library skips engine material: what leaves with the 12A is not parsed; the swap's documents move up to tier 2
body:
**The library skips engine material. Nothing that leaves with the 12A is parsed: the rotary itself, its carburettor and fuel delivery, emissions, ignition, charging and starting, cooling, exhaust, the 3N71B automatic, the propeller shaft and the A/C compressor. Everything about the car that stays is still read: body, body electrics, chassis, brakes, steering, suspension, wheels, interior, heating and the A/C system, and the fuel tank and its lines. So are the LS swap's own documents, which move up from tier 4 to 2.**

His words (chat, 2026-10-16): "also 00-library. please adjust the library plan to skip anything engine related and only preserve the other information about the car that stays relevant."

**Reading taken (CLAUDE.md §3).** "Engine related" is read as the engine and drivetrain that leave the car with the 12A (D-616, D-617). The LS swap's documents are about the engine that replaces it and "stay relevant", so they are kept, and they move up because the engine project now comes first (D-618). The fuel tank, its lines and its sender stay with the car, so their pages are read. The fuel pump, the carburettor and the regulator leave. The A/C system stays and only its compressor leaves (the LS drives its own, engine DS01).

**How it is done.** The rule lives in `build_queue.py`, which owns the queue (never edited by hand):
- `ENGINE_DOCS` names whole documents by path: the Weber, Carter, Holley, 3N71B and Sanden datasheets; the carburettor, rotary overhaul, Yamamoto and 1981 emissions books; the 1980 emissions, fuel-inlet-exhaust, engine-electrical and automatic sections; the 1985 engine, lubrication, cooling, engine-electrical, automatic and propeller-shaft sections; the 1980 compressor repair.
- In a mixed document a page is skipped when its topic names engine material (`ENGINE_TOPIC`) and nothing that stays (`KEEP_TOPIC` wins). Parts-catalogue groups 1000A to 2599A count as engine material.
- New items are born skipped. `--sweep` applies the rule to the queue as it stands, re-opens anything the rules stop calling engine material (one A/C bulletin, caught by "cooling" in the first sweep, was re-opened this way), and re-prices every open item by today's tier.
- Result: 406 items skipped, 823 open, about $27 predicted for what is left. A page whose topic is blank is still read: it cannot be told apart until an agent looks at it.

**Not changed.** The plan's phases (L2 still waits on his L8). The skipped documents' files stay where they are: the offline copy and the deletion (L5, L6) handle them like any other.

title: The BP's manuals are read first and the LS's skipped: Miata docs owner 01-engine tier 1, never skipped as engine material; claim and run_session take --owner
body:
**The library reads the BP's manuals first and the LS's not at all.**

- The Miata manuals go in 00-CAR/library/docs/miata-*: owner 01-engine, tier 1, scope other-model.
- Their pages are never skipped as engine material.
- Their items' brief tells the worker these are the swap's own engine and gearbox: take every fact as fully as for this car, applies=other-model, context naming the Miata year, never indexed.
- The LS swap's documents (03-cad's model/library/swap/, and 01-engine/cad/'s docs, oil-pan and transmission copies) are skipped as reference.
- rx7.py claim and run_session.py take --owner AREA, so a session can parse only one project's documents (--owner 01-engine).

His words, 2026-10-17, in chat: "now can you please. dial a plan for us today to gather as much information and make every detail of this plan, you should find all the possible manuals i could possibly need for the engine and for the transmission for rverything. when we have everydetail ebout both the transmission and the engine to deside what we perfect next (im thinking oil pan + lines). but first this is first gather every possible detail you can find about these parts from measurmetns specs sizes weights requiremnts bolt patters torque specs every servise prosedure the full owrks every detail"

**Why.**
- D-620 skipped engine pages because the 12A leaves. A Miata manual's engine pages would have been skipped by the same topic rule, and the BP is the engine he is buying (01-engine D-629).
- Tier 1 and --owner let the engine's pages be read before the car's backlog, without spending on the whole library.
- The LS documents would otherwise have taken engine sessions' money for an engine that is not coming.

**Sources** (00-CAR sources S-614 to S-622):
- On disk: the 1990 Miata workshop manual (Internet Archive) and the rusEFI 1994 pin-out.
- Behind a free account at mazdaclub.cz: the 1994 workshop manual (1,708 pages), the 1997 one and the 1994, 1995 and 1997 parts catalogues - 01-engine BP12.
- Forum dimensions and weights, to be replaced by measurements (BD15, R11).

Parsing still needs his go: 00-library L8. Merging stays the overhaul's (D-576), except what 01-engine BP03 takes into the engine's design from the staged facts.

title: The BP's manuals are read only where the swap needs them: the 1994 manual in four ranges, the 1990 scan skipped, the mellens sections whole
body:
**The BP's manuals are read only where the swap needs them.**

- The 1994 Miata manual (DOC-197, S-615) is three books in one PDF: the workshop manual, the body repair manual and the parts catalogue.
- Its pages are read in four ranges, found from its page labels and the catalogue's group numbers:
  - 1-401: general information, engine, lubrication, cooling, fuel and emission, engine electrical, clutch, manual transmission.
  - 582-585: the propeller shaft.
  - 1109-1140: technical data and special tools.
  - 1351-1456: the parts catalogue's groups 10-25, engine to propeller shaft.
- Skipped: the automatic, axles, steering, brakes, suspension, body, body electrical, HVAC, body repair and the chassis catalogue. They are the Miata's, not the swap's.
- The 1990 scan (DOC-164) is skipped whole: its engine is the 1.6, and the 1994 manual covers its gearbox with a text layer.
- The mellens.net 1994 and 1997 sections and the extras are read whole.

His words, 2026-10-17, in chat: "i could not find the manuals you refrenced on the website youreferenced but i found many 1994 manuals and a million more i dont wna to download them all please reverence https://www.mellens.net/mazda/ you should dinf every miata manual under the sun please compare with the listing to find the exact versin we have and strat pulling all the needed pdfs ot of that webside you should be able to download and if not read them and tell me acavtly which to download (the ones i downloaded already ae still in the downloads folder"

**Matching the listing.**
- BP-711698 is a 1994-97 NA BP, non-VVT. Which year it is (1994-95, cam sensor only; or 1996-97, OBD-II with a crank sensor) is BP01 and BD01.
- So both are kept: the 1994 manual and sections for the 1994-95 engine; the 1997 sections, the 1995-96 engine, the 1996 timing belt and the 1996 wiring for the later one; the 1990-97 supplement for both.
- The separate parts catalogues (S-617 to S-619) are not needed, since the 1994 PDF carries its own.

build_queue.py holds the rule (MIATA_KEEP). A range is widened there if a design finds a gap.
